open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows
open_points.text: one entry for each failing input or record, each naming the field or the identity it concerns; within one kind, entries are ordered first by the record or input they concern — inputs in the order the operation's Inputs list them, then records list by list in that same order, each list in its own order (A06) — and then, within one record or input, by its fields in the order its Inputs or model lists them.
open_points.question: When several fields of one input or record fail with the same error kind, is there one entry for that input or record, or one entry for each failing field?
options: One entry per failing input or record, carrying all of that subject's failing fields
One entry per failing field, so one input or record may produce several entries
open_points.default_guess: Emit one entry per failing field, grouped by input or record and ordered by field.

witness.initial: A valid owner session submits a project create with every required value present, but the embedded object has kind `villa` and floor area 0.
events: Stage (4) finds both object fields outside their allowed forms and no earlier stage fails.
outcomes: The refusal contains one failure entry for the object, grouping both bad fields.
The refusal contains two failure entries for the same object, one for kind and one for floor area.
witness.observer: The owner interface and any contract test comparing the refusal see a different number and shape of errors.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows
open_points.text: then records list by list in that same order, each list in its own order (A06)
open_points.question: What determines the order between two or more record lists whose failures have the same kind?
options: The order of list-valued fields in the operation's Inputs
The order in which the operation reads the lists
The order in which the operation's contract or Errors section names the record kinds
A separately declared record-list order for each operation
open_points.default_guess: Use an explicitly declared per-operation record-list order; where lists are inputs, default that declaration to their Inputs order.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows
open_points.text: within one record or input, by its fields in the order its Inputs or model lists them.
open_points.question: When a failing value is both an operation input and a model-shaped record, or contains a nested model, which field order takes precedence and how are nested fields flattened?
options: Use the operation's Inputs order throughout
Use the model's field order throughout
Use Inputs order for top-level inputs and recursively use each model's order for model fields
Require the operation to declare one flattened field order
open_points.default_guess: Use Inputs order for top-level inputs and recursively use the relevant model's order inside model-valued inputs.

open_points.subject: 50_public_apis_0_conventions.md:Conventions every operation follows
open_points.text: the next call is the first deadline at or after the reading when the pass can run again; a deadline equal to that reading is made.
open_points.question: Is “the reading when the pass can run again” a monotonic sample taken when the blocking call completes or the host resumes, or the scheduler's next actual clock sample after that event?
options: Sample immediately when the blocking condition ends and retain that reading for deadline selection
Use the scheduler's next actual monotonic reading
Treat every deadline crossed after the blocking condition ends but before the next scheduler reading as due
open_points.default_guess: Capture a monotonic reading when the blocking condition ends and make the first deadline at or after that captured reading.

witness.initial: Serving began at monotonic reading 0 with a 60-second pass interval; the call due at 60 runs until reading 119.9.
events: The previous call finishes at 119.9, so the pass can run again.
The scheduler next samples the clock at 120.1.
outcomes: Using the completion reading, deadline 120 is the first deadline at or after 119.9 and the next call is made when the scheduler runs at 120.1.
Using the scheduler's reading, deadline 120 is before 120.1 and is skipped; the next call is due at 180.
witness.observer: A timer test double, and any state cleaned up by that pass, observes whether the second call occurs near 120 or 180.
